correctness.rationale: An arbitrary rank-r idempotent is equivalent to complementary image/kernel subspaces; for fixed first projection, rank(EF)=p fixes dim(W∩K)=s-p. Fixing dim(W∩U)=h, a quotient-graph bijection gives exactly the image factor. A reference splitting V/W→V identifies complementary kernels with linear maps φ, whose projection to Hom(π(U),W/(U∩W)) has rank t-h exactly when rank(FE)=t, producing the remaining factors. All indices and nonnegative exponents are stated. A pure-Python checker exhaustively counts all ordered idempotent pairs in six (q,n) cases including GF(4), and separate normalized/swap checks test q=2,3,4,5,7,8 at n=5; computations corroborate, not replace, the all-prime-power proof. The image/kernel premise agrees with the fully inspected Theorem 2.1 of V. Pop (2016).

originality.rationale: The studied invariant is the joint, ordered quadruple-rank distribution of arbitrary pairs of idempotents in every full finite-field matrix algebra. Inspected primary literature establishes individual idempotent rank counts, semigroup-group structures, linear-combination rank identities or restricted similarity criteria; none of these statements implies the full Gaussian-binomial joint law without the new two-sided intersection and complement-map enumeration. No equal or dominating closed result was found. Bibliographic incompleteness is explicitly retained as a risk, not portrayed as proof of worldwide uniqueness.

Prior database retrieval is incomplete and does not establish global priority.

value.rationale: The distribution is the complete natural two-sided rank signature of product pairs inside the full linear monoid and of oblique projections in finite geometry. It captures the coupling ignored by single-product marginal ranks or individual idempotent counts, including positive asymmetric strata, and can be used as exact incidence data for random projection products and rank-relation questions. It covers all ranks, dimensions and extension fields with no artificial parameter cuts; the central novelty lies in the joint full-stratum count, not in recomputing a known Gaussian normalization.
